timeToProduction.text: A public connection works through its OAuth flow without a Marketplace listing. Marketplace listing is optional; Notion says to expect a reply within 5–10 business days.

verdict.summary: Notion has no OAuth scopes to get reviewed: users pick which pages to share in a page picker. Build a public connection for a 'Connect Notion' button. The Marketplace listing is optional and reviewed separately.

callouts.text: Choose the installation scope carefully: 'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only' can't be changed after the connection is created, and only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed on the Marketplace.
The docs note that the Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review. It's unclear how long that takes or whether approval is needed first; we didn't test it.

callouts.text: Each user authorizes separately. After one person installs a public connection, other members of the same workspace must go through the auth flow themselves.
Don't confuse this with Notion Workers' OAuth page: that one is about a Worker connecting to other providers (GitHub, Google) using PKCE, not about other apps connecting to Notion.

steps.title: Decide: personal token, internal connection, or public connection
steps.detail: Use a personal access token or internal connection to act in your own workspace. Use a public connection when other Notion users need to install your agent.

steps.title: Create a public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Fill in connection details, your redirect URI(s) under OAuth configuration, and the installation scope (can't be changed later).

steps.title: Store the client ID and secret as secrets
steps.detail: Copy them from the connection's Configuration tab into environment variables. Never put them in source code or version control.

steps.title: Build the authorize redirect
steps.detail: Send users to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, and a state value for CSRF protection.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.detail: POST to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET) and grant_type=authorization_code. Store access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id.

steps.title: Handle cancel and refresh
steps.detail: On cancel the redirect carries error=access_denied. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token; each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token.

steps.title: Test with your own workspace
steps.detail: Click Connect, share a page in the picker, and confirm an API call works on that page.

steps.title: (Optional) Draft a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Listing name and description, category and tags, images and logo, and the public connection to link. Save it as a draft.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit the listing and wait
steps.detail: Submit from Listings > Connections. Notion says to expect an email within 5–10 business days; if changes are needed, fix and resubmit.

noReview.why: Notion has no OAuth scopes. Users choose which pages and databases to share; parent pages share their children.
The consent prompt describes what the connection can do in the workspace. No review is tied to them in the pages we checked.

scopes.tip: Ask users to share only the pages your agent needs, or offer a template the connection duplicates and gets access to automatically.

scopeAdvisor.why: With a template, Notion adds the connection, duplicates the page and shares it with the connection automatically, so access stays narrow.

communityNotes.tip: An invalid_grant error from Notion's token endpoint can come from a redirect_uri that doesn't exactly match the one in the authorize URL. One developer's bug was a missing trailing slash.
